mainTopic: Female animals set aside for an עולה or an אשם, and the משנה's dispute over the substitute of an אשם, its offspring, and a leftover אשם.
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a challenge against רבי יוחנן. He had said that רבי יהושע's ruling on a female set aside as an עולה matches רבי שמעון's view on a female set aside as an אשם. The challenger objects that a female עולה is different, and that רבי שמעון himself says a female עולה can make a תמורה. רבי יוחנן answers that רבי יהושע follows another report of רבי שמעון, in which even a female עולה makes no תמורה. A new משנה then teaches what happens to the substitute of an אשם and its offspring, and to an אשם whose owner died or already got כפרה. The first opinion says they graze until blemished and are sold for communal gift offerings, רבי אליעזר says they are left to die, and רבי אלעזר says the money buys a private עולה. The גמרא explains why both cases were needed. It then discusses רב נחמן's statement about when the dispute applies, which רבא refutes and which ends with a קשיא. Finally רבי אבין בר חייא asks whether the offspring of a female set aside as an אשם can be an עולה. He is told yes, because it is fit to be offered, and he begins an objection from the משנה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A female burnt offering is different from a female guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: The challenger argues that רבי שמעון's lenient view applies only to an אשם, since a female אשם never exists. It cannot apply to an עולה, because a female עולה does exist in birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי שמעון only spoke about a female set aside for an אשם,] where its mother's kind never has the status of an אשם. But a female set aside for an עולה, where its mother's kind does have the status of an עולה, even רבי שמעון agrees [that it has real holiness].
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining a challenge already in progress against רבי יוחנן. The challenger says רבי שמעון's lenient view about a female אשם cannot be stretched to cover a female עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A female animal is never brought as an אשם, so a female set aside for one has no real holiness and is only worth its money. But female birds can be brought as an עולה, so a female set aside for an עולה is not so foreign to that offering. That means it may well have real holiness, even according to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: The status or 'name' of a guilt offering
A female animal set aside to be a burnt offering
Agrees or concedes
Literally 'on its mother', meaning its own gender or kind

steps.confusionAlert: 'Its mother' does not mean this animal's actual mother. It means an animal of the same gender, a female. The point is whether females of that kind can ever be this offering.

phrases.english: where there is no guilt-offering status on its mother,
phrases.notes: He means a female is never brought as an אשם, so 'its mother' stands for its gender.

phrases.english: but regarding a female set aside for a burnt offering
where there is burnt-offering status on its mother —
phrases.notes: Female birds can be brought as an עולה, so females are not completely excluded.

phrases.english: even Rabbi Shimon agrees!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל גַּבֵּי נְקֵבָה לְעוֹלָה דְּאִיכָּא שֵׁם עוֹלָה עַל אִמּוֹ אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge begun before this section against רבי יוחנן's linking of רבי יהושע to רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי יהושע (female for עולה is sold for שלמים) holds like רבי שמעון (female for אשם has no real holiness).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two cases differ. A female אשם never exists, but a female עולה does exist in birds, so רבי שמעון would agree a female עולה has real holiness.

steps.title: רבי שמעון says a female burnt offering can make a substitute
steps.stepSummary: A second objection: רבי שמעון is on record saying a female עולה does create a תמורה, which shows it has real holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, we have heard רבי שמעון say: with his female burnt offering, he does make a substitute!
steps.whatsHappening: The challenger adds a second, stronger objection. It quotes רבי שמעון's own words about a female עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only an animal with real body-holiness (קדושת הגוף) can create a תמורה. Since רבי שמעון says a female עולה creates a תמורה, he clearly holds it has real holiness. So he cannot be the source for selling it off as a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, which introduces an extra objection
Creates a substitute: swapping a regular animal for it makes the swapped animal holy
Holiness of the animal's body itself, not just of its money value

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, הָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: And furthermore, we have heard Rabbi Shimon say:
for his burnt offering, he makes a substitute!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד הָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection, based on an explicit ruling of רבי שמעון, to the logical objection of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's linking of רבי יהושע's view to רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Making a תמורה requires real holiness. רבי שמעון says a female עולה makes a תמורה, so to him it has real holiness, which contradicts the comparison.

steps.title: רבי יהושע follows another תנא's report of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that there is another report of רבי שמעון's view, from רבי שמעון בן יהודה. In that report, even a female עולה cannot create a תמורה, and רבי יהושע follows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי יהושע holds like the other תנא's version of רבי שמעון's opinion. As it was taught: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: even with his female burnt offering, he does not make a substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends his explanation. He points to a different report of what רבי שמעון held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two traditions about רבי שמעון. In the one quoted by רבי שמעון בן יהודה, a female עולה cannot make a תמורה, which means it has no real body-holiness, just like a female אשם. רבי יהושע follows that tradition, so both objections fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: The other תנא, meaning a different teacher of the tradition
According to the opinion of
Even

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reports of רבי שמעון's view on a female עולה. In one it makes a תמורה; in the other (רבי שמעון בן יהודה's) it does not. רבי יהושע follows the second, so רבי יוחנן's comparison stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: an apparent contradiction is solved by saying that two תנאים reported a sage's opinion differently.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר לֵיהּ
phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Yehoshua holds
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן answering the one who challenged him.

phrases.english: like the other tanna's view of Rabbi Shimon's opinion,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says
in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
even for his burnt offering, he does not make a substitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּאִידַּךְ תַּנָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both objections of steps 1 and 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different traditions of the same sage's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון holds that a female עולה has real holiness and makes a תמורה, so it cannot match רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון בן יהודה's report, רבי שמעון holds that even a female עולה makes no תמורה. רבי יהושע follows that view.

steps.title: New משנה: the substitute of a guilt offering and its offspring
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the substitute of an אשם, and all its offspring for every generation, are left to graze until they get a blemish. Then they are sold, and the money goes to communal gift offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The substitute of an אשם, the offspring of a substitute, their offspring, and their offspring's offspring until the end of time: they graze until they become blemished, then they are sold, and their money goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says what to do with the substitute of an אשם and with all the young born from such animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These animals cannot be offered as an אשם, but they are holy, so they cannot just be used. The solution is to wait until they get a blemish (מום), sell them, and use the money for voluntary communal offerings (נדבה).

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, which marks the start of a new משנה
An animal swapped for a guilt offering
Offspring, a newborn animal
They graze until they become blemished and unfit
Voluntary gift offerings, here communal ones

phrases.english: MISHNA: The substitute of a guilt offering,
the offspring of a substitute, their offspring, and the offspring of their offspring
until the end of all time —
they graze until they become blemished, and they are sold,
and their money goes to gift offerings.
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'its money' (the word in round brackets); the corrected wording, in square brackets, says 'their money.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ תְּמוּרַת אָשָׁם וְלַד תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unconnected to the preceding discussion about רבי שמעון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The substitute of an אשם and all its descendants graze until blemished, are sold, and the money goes to communal gift offerings.

steps.title: Two dissenting views in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says these animals are left to die. רבי אלעזר says the money from their sale is used to bring עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: they are left to die. And רבי אלעזר says: he should bring burnt offerings with its money.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings two sages who disagree with the first ruling, each in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר is stricter: there is no grazing and selling, and the animals are just left to die. רבי אלעזר agrees they are sold, but he disagrees about the money: it buys עולות rather than going to communal gift offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: They should be left to die
With its money, meaning the money from its sale
Burnt offerings

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two names! רבי אליעזר (with a yud) says the animals die. רבי אלעזר (without it) says the money buys עולות.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views: the first opinion says graze, sell, and the money goes to communal gift offerings. רבי אליעזר says the animals are left to die. רבי אלעזר says sell them and bring עולות with the money.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: they are left to die.
And Rabbi Elazar says:
he should bring burnt offerings with its money.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר יָמוּתוּ וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר יָבִיא בִּדְמֵיהּ עוֹלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two dissenting opinions to the first ruling of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the animals are left to die. רבי אלעזר: the money from their sale buys עולות.

steps.title: A leftover אשם: three opinions again
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a second case, an אשם whose owner died or already gained כפרה, and repeats the three-way dispute: sell it for communal gift offerings, let it die, or bring a private עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אשם whose owner died, or whose owner already gained atonement, grazes until it gets a blemish. Then it is sold, and the money goes to gift offerings. רבי אליעזר says: they are left to die. רבי אלעזר says: he brings an עולה with its money.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new case of an אשם that can no longer be offered, and the same three opinions from the earlier case show up again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the dispute was about the תמורה of an אשם and its offspring. Now the case is the אשם itself, when its owner died or already got כפרה with another animal. The חכמים send the money to communal gift offerings, רבי אליעזר lets it die, and רבי אלעזר has the owner bring his own private עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A guilt offering whose owner died
Whose owner already gained atonement with a different animal
They become blemished, so they can no longer be offered
Gift offering; here it means the communal burnt offerings paid for from leftover funds
They are left to die

phrases.english: A guilt offering whose owner died,
and one whose owner already gained atonement —
they graze until they become blemished,
and they are sold, and the money goes to gift offerings.
Rabbi Eliezer says: they are left to die.
Rabbi Elazar says:
he should bring a burnt offering with its money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָשָׁם שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלָיו, וְשֶׁכִּיפְּרוּ בְּעָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same three-way dispute from steps 4-5 to a new case: the leftover אשם itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per the חכמים, a leftover אשם grazes until blemished, is sold, and the money goes to communal gift offerings. רבי אליעזר says it dies. רבי אלעזר says the owner brings a private עולה with the money.

steps.title: What is the difference between רבי אלעזר and the חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks: a gift offering is also an עולה, so how is רבי אלעזר's view any different from the חכמים?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't a gift offering also an עולה? So what is the difference between the words of רבי אלעזר and the words of the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה stops to ask what the real difference is between two opinions that look the same. This sets up the answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים send the money to gift offerings, and those gift offerings are burnt offerings. רבי אלעזר also says to bring an עולה. So on the surface, both opinions end with an עולה, and the משנה wants to know what they actually disagree about.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a question that points out something obvious)
What is the difference between
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: But isn't a gift offering also a burnt offering?
So what is the difference between the words of Rabbi Elazar
and the words of the Sages?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא אַף נְדָבָה עוֹלָה הִיא, וּמָה בֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the two opinions in step 6 actually differ in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference is there between רבי אלעזר's עולה and the חכמים' gift offering, since both are burnt offerings?

steps.title: A private עולה: the owner's role
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי אלעזר, the animal is the owner's private עולה. He leans his hands on it, pays for its נסכים, and if he is a כהן, he gets the service and the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when it comes as an עולה, the owner leans his hands on it and brings נסכים, and the נסכים are paid for by him. If he was a כהן, its service and its hide are his.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts its answer by describing a private עולה, which is what רבי אלעזר means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is who owns the offering. In רבי אלעזר's view it is the owner's own personal עולה. So he does סמיכה, he pays for the נסכים, and if he is a כהן, he gets to do the service and keep the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: Leans his hands on the animal (סְמִיכָה), done by the owner of a private offering
The wine offerings, along with the flour offering, that go with a קרבן
Its service, meaning the right to perform the offering
Its hide, which goes to the כהן

phrases.english: Rather, when it comes as a burnt offering —
phrases.notes: This means his own private burnt offering, which is רבי אלעזר's view.

phrases.english: he leans his hands on it,
and he brings libations,
and its libations come from his own property.
If he was a priest —
its service and its hide are his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא בָּאָה עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 7's question by describing a private עולה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר means a private עולה. The owner does סמיכה, pays for the נסכים, and if he is a כהן, he gets the service and the hide.

steps.title: A communal gift offering: the owner has no special role
steps.stepSummary: Under the חכמים, the animal is a communal offering. The owner does no סמיכה, the community pays for the נסכים, and even if he is a כהן, the service and hide go to the כהנים on duty that week.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when it is a gift offering, he does not lean on it and does not bring נסכים for it. Its נסכים come from the community. Even if he is a כהן, its service and its hide belong to the men of the משמר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its answer by describing the communal gift offering, which is what the חכמים mean. This completes the contrast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the חכמים' view the money becomes community property, so the original owner loses all personal connection to the offering. That is why he does no סמיכה and does not pay for the נסכים. Even if he is a כהן, he has no special right to the service or the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: The community; communal offerings are paid for from public funds
The group of כהנים on duty in the בית המקדש that week
Even though

steps.whatToRemember: Both views end with an עולה. The difference is ownership: for רבי אלעזר it is the owner's private עולה, with סמיכה, his own נסכים, and the כהן's rights. For the חכמים it is a communal offering, with none of these.

phrases.english: And when it is a gift offering —
phrases.notes: This means a communal gift offering, which is the חכמים' view.

phrases.english: he does not lean his hands on it,
and he does not bring libations for it,
and its libations come from the community,
even though he is a priest —
its service and its hide belong to the men of the priestly watch.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁהִיא נְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast begun in step 8 by describing the communal offering.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים mean a communal offering: no סמיכה, the נסכים come from the community, and the service and hide go to the כהנים on duty, even if the owner is a כהן.

steps.title: The גמרא opens: both disputes are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by saying that the משנה needed to teach the dispute in both cases, the תמורה of an אשם and the leftover אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts, and its first move is to say that both disputes in the משנה had to be taught. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה repeated the same three opinions in two different cases. A learner might think one case would have been enough. The גמרא says no, both are needed, and it is about to explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
It is necessary; used to show that two teachings that look alike are both needed

phrases.english: Gemara: And it is necessary:

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא, which begins by justifying why the משנה repeats the dispute in two cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both disputes in the משנה are necessary, and neither could be learned from the other.

steps.title: If only the leftover guilt offering were taught
steps.stepSummary: Had the משנה taught only the leftover אשם, we might think רבי אליעזר says 'let it die' only there, because of a גזירה. For a תמורת אשם he might agree with the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה had only taught the case of the leftover אשם, we would think that only there רבי אליעזר says the animal must die. His reason would be a rabbinic decree: he forbids using an אשם after כפרה, so people won't confuse it with an אשם before כפרה. But for the substitute of an אשם and the offspring of that substitute, we might think he agrees with the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the first half of why both cases are needed. If only the אשם case were taught, we might wrongly limit רבי אליעזר's harsh view to that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's 'let them die' could be explained by a special decree that only fits a real אשם. The worry is that people would mix up an אשם after כפרה with one before כפרה. A תמורה or its offspring is never offered as an אשם anyway, so that worry would not apply, and we might think he agrees with the רבנן there.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught us (the משנה told us this case)
He made a rabbinic decree
After the owner already got atonement
Because of / out of concern for
The offspring of its substitute animal

phrases.english: For if it had taught us only the guilt offering,
in this case Rabbi Eliezer says they should die,
because he made a decree about after atonement
on account of before atonement.
phrases.notes: He worries people would treat an אשם before atonement the same way, when that one must really be used for an אשם.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל גַּבֵּי תְּמוּרַת אָשָׁם, וְלַד תְּמוּרָתָהּ,
phrases.english: But regarding the substitute of a guilt offering and the offspring of its substitute,
I would say he agrees with the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן אָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of the צריכותא announced in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taught alone, the אשם case would suggest רבי אליעזר's view rests on a decree that does not reach the תמורה case.

steps.title: If only the substitute were taught, so both cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: Had the משנה taught only the תמורה case, we might think the רבנן are lenient only there and agree with רבי אליעזר about the leftover אשם. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had only taught the case of the substitute, we would think that only there the רבנן say it goes out to graze. But for an actual אשם, they would agree with רבי אליעזר that it must die. That is why both cases are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of the reasoning and concludes that the משנה needed to teach both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry now runs the other way. The רבנן's lenient view could seem to fit only the תמורה, where there is no reason for a decree. For a real אשם, they might accept רבי אליעזר's decree. Teaching both cases shows the dispute is the same in each.

keyTerms.meaning: There (the other case, the תמורה)
They agree / concede
It is necessary (both cases had to be taught)

steps.whatToRemember: A צריכותא shows that each case teaches something the other could not. Here both cases show that רבי אליעזר and the רבנן hold their views consistently.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the substitute and its offspring.

phrases.english: in this case the Rabbis say their view,
phrases.notes: Their view is that the animals go out to graze.

phrases.english: but regarding a guilt offering
they agree with Rabbi Eliezer —
therefore it is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא begun in Steps 10 and 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both cases are needed. Each one, taught alone, could have suggested that one side concedes in the other case.

steps.title: The dispute applies only after atonement
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says the dispute applies only after כפרה. Before כפרה, everyone agrees the animal itself is offered as an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the argument is only about after the owner got atonement. But before atonement, everyone agrees that the animal itself is offered as an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement from an אמורא limits when the dispute in the משנה applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is about the offspring of a תמורת אשם, the case from the first part of the משנה. The fight between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן only applies once the owner already got כפרה. Before that, both sides agree that the offspring itself can be brought as an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: The dispute
Before the owner got atonement
Everyone agrees
Will be offered on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue in every situation. According to רב נחמן, before כפרה they agree completely.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
The dispute is after atonement,
but before atonement —
everyone agrees
that it itself is offered as a guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the צריכותא ends, a new אמורא statement limits the scope of the משנה's dispute.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the boundary of the whole dispute. רבא challenges this claim in the next step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute applies only after כפרה. Before כפרה, all agree the animal itself is offered as an אשם.

steps.title: רבא gives two refutations
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the earlier statement with two arguments: no כפרה through a דבר הבא בעבירה, and רב חנניא's teaching that a second offspring is not offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There are two refutations of this statement. First, a person cannot get atonement through something that came from a transgression. Second, רב חנניא taught a ברייתא supporting רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said the first offspring is offered but the second offspring is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's statement from the last step. He says the animal cannot be offered at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is the offspring of a תמורה, and making a תמורה is forbidden. So it came from an עבירה and cannot bring כפרה. It is also two generations away from the original קרבן, and רב חנניא taught that such a 'second offspring' is not offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Two refutations, two answers against a claim
Something that came about through a sin
Gets atonement
First offspring (the קרבן's own young) / second offspring (the young of that young)
To support (someone's opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two refutations. The first is about how the animal came about (through a forbidden תמורה). The second is about distance: it is two generations away from the original קרבן.

phrases.english: Rava said: There are two refutations of this matter,
one, that a person does not achieve atonement
through something that comes from a transgression,
phrases.notes: Making a תמורה is forbidden, so an animal born from a תמורה traces back to a sin.

phrases.english: and furthermore, didn't Rav Chananya teach
in support of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
who said: the first offspring is offered,
but the second offspring is not offered!
phrases.notes: The 'second offspring' is the young of the young. The offspring of a תמורה is treated the same way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁתֵּי תְּשׁוּבוֹת בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's statement in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה, claiming the animal itself can be offered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animal came from an עבירה, and it counts as a 'second offspring,' which רב חנניא taught is not offered

steps.title: A new version of רב נחמן's statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rephrases the statement: the dispute is before כפרה, but after כפרה the animal itself is brought as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The dispute is before atonement. But after atonement, the animal itself is offered as an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of רבא's attack, the גמרא gives a corrected version of רב נחמן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the owner's כפרה, רבי אליעזר worries the animal might be wrongly brought as an אשם, so he says it dies, and the חכמים disagree. After the original אשם is brought, that worry is gone, so everyone agrees the animal can be an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (a corrected version of a statement)
Before the owner's atonement through his אשם
After the atonement has been done
Burnt offering, burned entirely on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a third opinion. It is the same statement of רב נחמן, retold in a corrected form.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabbah bar Avuh said:
The dispute is before atonement,
phrases.notes: This is the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים about the offspring of a תמורה.

phrases.english: but after atonement,
it itself is offered as a burnt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִי אִיתְּמַר, הָכִי אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the version of the statement that רבא refuted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was located elsewhere, and the animal was said to be offered in a case רבא rejected
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is before כפרה. After כפרה everyone agrees the animal is brought as an עולה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After כפרה, the offspring of a תמורת אשם is itself offered as an עולה

steps.title: רב חנניא's teaching still contradicts it
steps.stepSummary: The new version is challenged by רב חנניא's ברייתא about the second offspring, and the גמרא admits it is difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב חנניא teach a ברייתא supporting רבי יהושע בן לוי? It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבא's second refutation against the new version and admits there is no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the dispute to before כפרה does not help. The new version still says the animal is brought as an עולה, and it is still a 'second offspring,' which רב חנניא taught is not offered. The word קשיא means the problem stays unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult. The question stands without an answer, but the statement is not fully thrown out.

steps.whatToRemember: Even the corrected version of רב נחמן's statement stays a קשיא because of רב חנניא's teaching that a second offspring is not offered.
steps.confusionAlert: A bare קַשְׁיָא is weaker than תיובתא. The גמרא is admitting a difficulty, not declaring the opinion fully refuted.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chananya teach
in support of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi!
phrases.notes: This is the same teaching from step 14: the second offspring is not offered.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתָנֵי רַב חֲנַנְיָא לְסַיּוֹעֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the corrected version from step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that after כפרה the animal itself is brought as an עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is a second offspring, and רב חנניא taught a second offspring is not offered

steps.title: Can the offspring of a female set aside as an אשם be an עולה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין בר חייא asks: if a female was set aside as an אשם, can her offspring be brought as an עולה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין בר חייא asked רבי אבין בר כהנא: If someone set aside a female as an אשם, can her offspring be offered as an עולה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens a new topic: the offspring of a female animal that was set aside as an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם must be a male, so a female set aside for it cannot be offered as an אשם. The question is whether her young can be used for a different קרבן, an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside an animal for a קרבן
Female animal
Guilt offering, which must be a male

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin bar Chiyya asked
Rabbi Avin bar Kahana:
If one set aside a female for a guilt offering,
what is the law: may her offspring be offered as a burnt offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר חִיָּיא מֵרַבִּי אָבִין בַּר כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the previous discussion ended with a קשיא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the offspring of a female set aside as an אשם may be offered as an עולה

steps.title: Why not settle it from רבי יוסי's statement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the question was needed, since רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא already said that רבי אלעזר agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him settle it from the statement of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who said: רבי אלעזר agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question itself: an earlier statement already seems to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said that רבי אלעזר agrees in this case that the offspring is not offered. If that is already known, there should be nothing left to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him resolve it (from a known source)
Agrees, concedes

phrases.english: But let him resolve it
from the statement of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina,
who said: Rabbi Elazar concedes.
phrases.notes: He means רבי אלעזר agrees in this case that the offspring is not offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפְשׁוֹט לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why step 17's question was needed
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי אבין בר חייא's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known statement of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא already answers it

steps.title: He had not heard it
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבי אבין בר חייא had never heard רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had not heard it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the question was real, because the asker did not know the earlier statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was not pointless. The person asking simply did not know the earlier statement. The גמרא now goes back to the question to report the answer he was given.

keyTerms.meaning: He had not heard it

steps.whatToRemember: When the גמרא says לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ, it is only explaining why someone asked the question: he did not know the earlier statement.

phrases.english: He had not heard it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: The asker did not know the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was unnecessary because רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא already settled it
steps.terutzMaskana: The question was real for the asker, since he had not heard that statement

steps.title: The answer: the offspring is brought as an עולה
steps.stepSummary: Returning to רבי אבין בר חייא's question, he is told that the offspring of a female set aside as an אשם is offered as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? He said to him: its offspring is brought as an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי אבין בר חייא's question from before and gives the answer he received: the offspring is brought as an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was about a female set aside as an אשם. A female cannot be an אשם, but her male offspring can be offered. The answer says that offspring goes up on the מזבח as an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Her offspring (here, the male born to the female animal)
Is offered as an עולה (a burnt offering)

phrases.english: What [is the law]?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is picking up רבי אבין בר חייא's question from earlier, after the short side discussion.

phrases.english: He said to him: its offspring is brought as an עולה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the question of Step 17 now that Steps 18-19 explained why it was asked.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The offspring of a female set aside as an אשם is offered as an עולה.

steps.title: Pushback: רבי אלעזר only spoke about a female set aside as an עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין בר חייא challenges the answer. רבי אלעזר allowed the offspring as an עולה only when the mother herself was set aside as an עולה. With an אשם, the mother never had the status of an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this? רבי אלעזר only said this when someone sets aside a female for an עולה, because the status of עולה is on its mother. But with an אשם, where there is no status of עולה on its mother, even רבי אליעזר agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner pushes back on the answer. He says the case of an אשם is different from the case רבי אלעזר discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the עולה case, the mother already had the name 'עולה', so it makes sense that her offspring becomes an עולה. In the אשם case, the mother was never called an עולה, so there seems to be no reason to make her offspring one. Here, he says, everyone would agree the offspring is not offered.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? (a way of rejecting what was just said)
He only said this much and no more (it limits a ruling to its own case)
The name or status of an עולה
Agrees

phrases.english: What is this?

phrases.aramaic: עַד כַּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar only said [this]
when one sets aside a female for an עולה,
since there is the status of עולה on its mother,
but regarding an אשם,
where there is no status of עולה on its mother —
even Rabbi Eliezer agrees!
phrases.notes: He means that in this case everyone would agree the offspring is not offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי? עַד כַּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the offspring of a female set aside as an אשם is offered as an עולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר's ruling depends on the mother already having עולה status. That is missing when the mother was set aside as an אשם.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's real reason: the offspring is fit to be offered
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבי אלעזר's reason is not the mother's עולה status. His reason is that the offspring is fit to be offered, and that is true in the אשם case too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי אלעזר's reason is not because of the status of עולה on its mother. It is because the offspring is fit to be offered, and this one is also fit to be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The answerer defends his ruling by explaining what רבי אלעזר's reason really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that רבי אלעזר relied on the mother's name 'עולה'. The answer moves the reason: what counts is that the male offspring can be offered on the מזבח. Since the male born to the אשם-female can also be offered, the same ruling applies.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
Fit to be offered on the מזבח
And this one also

steps.whyThisMatters: It changes the basis of רבי אלעזר's ruling from the mother's status to the offspring's own fitness. That lets the ruling reach the אשם case.

phrases.english: He said to him: the reason of Rabbi Elazar

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּשֵׁם עוֹלֶה עַל אִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: is not because the status of עולה is on its mother,
but because it is fit to be offered,
and this one is also fit to be offered.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the male born to the female that was set aside as an אשם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, לָאו מִשּׁוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the reason behind רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's ruling depends on the mother having עולה status, so it would not apply to an אשם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling depends on the offspring being fit to be offered, which is true in the אשם case as well.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: only 'with their money'
steps.stepSummary: An objection is raised from the משנה. There, רבי אלעזר says that with the money from these offspring, for all generations, one brings an עולה. The גמרא begins to read it closely: with their money, yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection to him: their offspring, and the offspring of their offspring until the end of the world, he brings an עולה with their money. With their money, yes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins, quoted from the משנה. The גמרא starts making an inference from its exact words, and the inference is finished in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אלעזר says the עולה is bought 'with their money', meaning the animals are sold and the money used. That suggests the offspring themselves are not offered. This goes against the claim that the offspring is fit to be offered as an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Their offspring
Until the end of time (every future generation)
With their money (the money from selling them)
Yes

steps.confusionAlert: The step is not finished. 'With their money, yes' is the first half of an inference. The other half, that the animal itself is not offered, comes next.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
their offspring, and the offspring of their offspring
until the end of the world —
he brings an עולה with their money.
With their money — yes,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: וְלָדָן וְלַד וְלָדָן עַד סוֹף כׇּל הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 22 using the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the offspring of a female set aside as an אשם is itself offered as an עולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the עולה is brought 'with their money'. This implies the offspring are sold, not offered themselves.
